answer.sameness: Most pages use the same thin header, left-aligned headline and short paragraph, followed by either a right-hand photograph or a sparse outline illustration. Heavy sans-serif headlines dominate seven pages; the watchmaker, winery and cheesemaker provide serif variations. Architecture, grooming and glazing share an especially similar white-and-blue split layout. Brewery, dance, cheese and watches repeat the dark-background-plus-line-art formula. Mobile repeats boxed menu buttons and bottom contact bars, with content largely rearranged into a single stack.
recurringIssues: Several mobile screens give large decorative illustrations or empty space priority over useful content, pushing information and actions toward the bottom edge.
Business identity relies too heavily on a generic category symbol rather than distinctive photography, materials or visual detail.
Small body text and tiny desktop controls create a pronounced gap between oversized headlines and secondary information.
The optician's dark text on saturated blue and the watchmaker's very faint clock drawing show inconsistent contrast control.
Visible AI-generation badges on the architecture, grooming and glazing photographs make the presentation feel unfinished.

best.why: The forest-green and yellow palette, expressive serif headline and prominent telephone number form the clearest, most cohesive identity across both sizes.
The step diagram gives the page a relevant visual idea, while the red accents clearly distinguish registration from secondary contact information.
The overlapping architectural and landscape images introduce depth and a sense of place that most of the other compositions lack.

weakest.why: The heavy blue service block has poor text contrast, and the additional blue strip on mobile makes the composition look unresolved.
A large, nearly empty pale hero and tiny vineyard drawing provide little visual atmosphere, especially on mobile where the main area feels underfilled.
Repeated business identification, a detached address block and an oversized abstract bend produce a fragmented hierarchy without a convincing cycling identity.

answer.oneChange: Require a genuinely business-specific hero concept before layout begins, varying composition and using credible imagery or bespoke graphics instead of repeatedly pairing a headline with a category icon.
answer.summary: This is competent template-shop work with a few stronger identities, not yet a distinctive studio portfolio. Colour and illustration subjects change more than the underlying design logic. The cheesemaker and dance school show how a coherent visual idea can help, while the optician, winery and bike service expose weak hierarchy and underdeveloped heroes. Mobile layouts need more deliberate control of decorative space and content order. Invest in business-specific art direction rather than producing further palette-and-symbol variations.
